name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,147

clue.text: Engrossed in deaf cats barking

indicators.note: 'barking' is slang for mad, so the letters before it have gone crazy and must be rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, ten letters including the little word 'in'

explanation.surface: Someone is absorbed in the din of cats that cannot hear themselves yowling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' reads as a link word joining 'Engrossed' to the cats, but it is part of the fodder: without it the count falls two short of ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Being engrossed means your attention is completely held, just as when something has you spellbound.

clue.text: Gross gangster Capone causing death

blocks.note: gross in the sense of obese
Al Capone, the Chicago mobster

explanation.surface: A Prohibition-era mobster's crude violence proves deadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gross' looks like it means disgusting, matching the gangster; here it means overweight.
explanation.definitionFit: A fatal wound or accident is one that kills, a direct dictionary synonym.

clue.text: Some crooks allied for theft ventured out

indicators.note: 'Some' of the following words means only part of their run of letters is taken

blocks.note: runs from the tail of 'crooks' to the start of 'theft'

explanation.surface: A gang of thieves team up and head off on a heist.
explanation.walkthrough: SALLIED FORTH sits across four words, starting with the last letter of 'crooks' and ending with the first two of 'theft'.
explanation.definitionFit: To sally forth is an old-fashioned idiom for setting off boldly on an outing or expedition.

clue.text: Bird is consuming odd bits of Brie

indicators.note: 'odd bits' asks for the letters in the first, third and other odd places of the cheese
to consume is to take in, so the short word 'is' swallows the cheese's letters

blocks.note: used as it stands, split around the inner letters
first and third letters of the cheese

explanation.surface: A bird is pecking at a wedge of soft French cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: The chosen letters of Brie go inside 'is', between its I and S, to give IBIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged wading bird with a curved bill, an example of the category.

clue.text: Fought guard desperately protecting earl

indicators.note: acting desperately means acting wildly, so the letters of 'guard' are thrown into disorder
to protect is to surround, so the jumbled guard wraps around the nobleman

blocks.note: anagram fodder
E is the standard abbreviation for earl

explanation.surface: A bodyguard battles frantically to shield an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: GUARD rearranges to ARGUD, and E slips in before the final D.
explanation.definitionFit: Fought here means had a verbal quarrel, and people who quarrel have a dispute with words.

clue.text: Desires — wanting top pay

indicators.note: 'wanting' means lacking, so the word for desires is missing its top, which in a down clue is its first letter

blocks.note: longings or cravings

explanation.surface: An employee longs for the highest possible salary.
explanation.walkthrough: YEARNINGS drops its Y; in a down answer the first letter is the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Your pay is the money you receive for work, which is what your wages and salary amount to.

clue.text: Renovated large manor of departmental boss

indicators.note: a renovated house has been rebuilt and rearranged, so the following letters are reordered

blocks.note: anagram fodder, twelve letters

explanation.surface: A company executive has had a grand country house done up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' looks like a link word, but its two letters are needed to reach twelve.
explanation.definitionFit: In a department store, the person in charge of one sales floor or department supervises its staff.

clue.text: Shellfish gobbled up by egret’s young

indicators.note: something gobbled is inside, so the answer lies within the words that follow 'by'
in a down clue 'up' means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

blocks.note: the run from inside 'egret's' into 'young', read forwards

explanation.surface: A heron's chick swallows a mollusc from the shallows.
explanation.walkthrough: Ignore the apostrophe: egRET'S YOung holds RETSYO, which reads OYSTER going upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The oyster is a bivalve mollusc, an example of seafood that lives in a shell.

clue.text: Significant Swiss folk hero, in Geneva originally

indicators.note: 'originally' points to the origin, the very first letter, of the Swiss city

blocks.note: William Tell, the legendary crossbowman who shot an apple off his son's head
used as it stands
first letter of the city

explanation.surface: A legendary Swiss hero has an important link with Geneva.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Significant' looks like praise for the hero but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A telling detail is revealing and meaningful, one that carries weight or importance.

clue.text: Reset switch

blocks.note: to lay something again, such as carpet or bricks
an electrically operated switch in a circuit

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is RE-LAY, to put down again; the second is the electrical component.
explanation.definitionFit: Re-laying a floor sets it again; a relay is a device that opens or closes a circuit remotely.

clue.text: Scottish landowner ultimately overlooked den of wild animal

indicators.note: the landowner's last letter is ignored, so the word is cut short at its end

blocks.note: the Scots word for the owner of a large estate

explanation.surface: A Scottish estate owner gazes down on a wild creature's hideout.
explanation.walkthrough: A laird is a Scottish landed proprietor; drop his final D.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is the resting place or hideaway where a wild beast sleeps.

clue.text: Place to land aircraft here briefly organised with pilot

indicators.note: 'briefly' means cut short, so the word before it loses its last letter
things that are organised have been put in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the word 'here' without its final E
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A pilot arranges to set down here for a short stop.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs to 'aircraft', leaving HER plus PILOT to be shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: A heliport is an airfield built for helicopters to take off and touch down.

clue.text: Final has to be rearranged immediately

indicators.note: the letters are told outright that they must be put into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, eight letters

explanation.surface: A cup final must be rescheduled at short notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' reads as the verb of the sentence but is fodder alongside 'Final'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in a flash happens instantly, an idiom for very quickly.

clue.text: Burdened boy with case for excursion

indicators.note: a case is the outside of something, so only the outer letters of the trip word are kept

blocks.note: a lad is a boy
first and last letters of the word for a trip

explanation.surface: A boy lugs a heavy suitcase on a day trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks like luggage in the surface, but it means the outside letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means heavily loaded or weighed down, a direct synonym of carrying a heavy load.

clue.text: Drank apple rum with daughter

indicators.note: 'rum' is an old word for odd or strange, so the fruit's letters come out in a strange order

blocks.note: anagram fodder
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Someone and their daughter knocked back some apple-flavoured spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink but is the anagram indicator, meaning odd.
explanation.definitionFit: To lap is to drink by scooping liquid with the tongue, as a cat does with milk.

clue.text: One playing in the morning in Germany

indicators.note: the time-of-day abbreviation sits in the abbreviation for the country

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for Germany
a.m., before noon

explanation.surface: A musician performs at breakfast time while touring Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' tempts you toward a musician or athlete; the answer is simply one who plays games.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamer is someone who plays video or tabletop games, so a player of them.

clue.text: Sensual books penned by Scandinavian fellow

indicators.note: something penned by a man is enclosed as if in a pen, so his name goes around the books

blocks.note: a Norse name, as in Eric the Red
the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A Nordic author has written some steamy novels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned' looks like writing, fitting the books, but here it means enclosed as in a pen; Eric the Red was a Norse explorer.
explanation.definitionFit: Erotic describes something arousing sexual desire, closely matching the bodily pleasure of sensual.

clue.text: University don of leprosy regularly lost volunteers

indicators.note: every other letter of the phrase is dropped at regular intervals, leaving the rest

blocks.note: short for professor, a senior academic
second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters, the odd ones having been lost

explanation.surface: An academic lost his research subjects in a study of leprosy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'volunteers' looks like a plural noun for people who offer help; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To proffer is to hold out or offer something freely, which is what someone who volunteers does.

clue.text: Open a French party

blocks.note: the French word for 'a'
a do is a party or social event

explanation.surface: Someone launches a party in France.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'do' is informal British English for a party or celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo a knot, button or parcel is to unfasten it, so to open it.

clue.text: Frequently become less harsh after leader’s gone

indicators.note: once the leader has gone, the first letter of the verb is removed

blocks.note: to grow gentler

explanation.surface: Regimes tend to grow milder once the dictator has departed.
explanation.walkthrough: SOFTEN minus its S.
explanation.definitionFit: Often and frequently are direct synonyms meaning many times or repeatedly.

clue.text: See disheartened side be defeated

indicators.note: a thing without heart has its middle removed, so only the outside letters of the team word remain

blocks.note: 'lo', as in 'lo and behold', means see
the team word with its middle letters removed

explanation.surface: Watch a demoralised team go down to defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' belongs to 'side', not 'See': LO plus S(ID)E.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose a match is to be beaten by the opposition, the opposite of winning.

clue.text: Additional painting by European returned

indicators.note: something returned comes back the way it went, so the whole string is read backwards

blocks.note: painting as a form of art
the multiplication sign, as in 'three by four'
E is the standard abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A further picture by a European artist has been sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' looks like a link or an artist's credit; it is the times sign X.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means more than usual or supplementary, the same as added on.

clue.text: Considered shutting hotel in difficult time

indicators.note: to shut something in is to enclose it, so the hard word surrounds the hotel letter

blocks.note: hard
T is the standard abbreviation for time
H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hotel was deliberating on closing during a tough period.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes inside TOUGH, then T is added: T(H)OUGH + T.
explanation.definitionFit: Considered as a past-tense verb means pondered or believed, as does its synonym here.

clue.text: Scared, flee bird enclosure

blocks.note: cowardly, as in 'too chicken to try'
run away

explanation.surface: A frightened creature bolts from a fenced pen.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer describes itself: a scared hen fleeing her coop.
explanation.definitionFit: A chicken run is a fenced outdoor yard where poultry are kept.
